# P11 development question on archived rubric scores

Can row-specific agreement between an automated panel and two instructors improve a forecast of the third instructor's four released analytic scores? Use all 38 writers, both tasks and each of the three instructor rotations in Campbell's public deposit, version 19656187. Omit holistic scores derived by Facets, student attributes and essay text. Each development writer's two tasks and all assessor rotations are excluded together from fitting. This is a retrospective annotation-prediction endpoint; there is no third-rater intervention or observation of grading time.

Predict each criterion with the equally weighted mean of two observed instructors. Fit the average residual for the held-out instructor identity and criterion using other writers, with eight zero-residual pseudo-observations for regularization. For a second independently calibrated forecast, average the four archived AI scores and apply the same correction. The candidate blends the two corrected predictions using inverse estimates of mean squared error learned from the other writers. Estimate errors separately for task, instructor and criterion, further conditioned on whether the two available instructors differ by at least one score point. Shrink conditional error sums with eight observations at the unconditional stratum MSE. Exclude each training writer when computing their residual corrections for weight training. Controls are the two-instructor mean, corrected instructor estimate, individual raters' extremes (min/max), raw and corrected automated mean, a constant half mixture and the same blend without the disagreement split. All approaches see the same observed score set when appropriate; the component ablation isolates the gating hypothesis.

Primary endpoint is MAE averaged equally over observations within writer and then writers. Use 10,000 paired writer bootstraps, seed 407, with Bonferroni percentile intervals across eight contrasts. Screen at .05 score-point gain and a positive simultaneous lower endpoint against every control. This is a new threshold for this development question, separate from the original rubric-reliability threshold. Restrict implications to these published scores; no independent historical-reasoning rubric validation is available here.
